title: Grade against a rubric, assembled
sub: An independent reviewer, who never sees the grader's reasoning, catches a misread rubric line before it becomes a grade.

nodes.l: Check every quote against the text

steps.d:
A short essay on extending the lunch period, four rubric criteria: thesis,
evidence, counterargument, organization

steps.h: The grader scores every criterion, with a quote for each
steps.d:
thesis: 1 · evidence: 1 · counterargument: 3, quoted "I don't really
have a counterargument because everyone agrees lunch should be
longer anyway" · organization: 1

steps.h: Code checks every quote against the submission, verbatim
steps.d:
all four quotes found in the text; none dropped as unevidenced
(the counterargument quote is real -- it is just not evidence
of what the rubric asks for)

steps.h: The reviewer, independently, decides what to check
steps.d:
→ CHECK: counterargument
(the reviewer has not seen the grader's reasoning, only
the submission, the rubric and these four proposed scores)

steps.h: Code returns that criterion's full rubric text and the submission again
steps.d:
counterargument (0-4 points): describes a real opposing position
accurately and responds to it, rather than dismissing it or
asserting that no one holds it -- level 0: no opposing position
appears anywhere in the essay

steps.h: The reviewer rejects, naming the criterion
steps.d:
"REJECT: counterargument scores 3 but the quote never states
an opposing position, it only claims no one holds one, which
the rubric's level 0 describes, not level 3."
